html:
The Manufahi revolt of 1911 and 1912 was the largest uprising against Portuguese rule in Timor, led by Dom Boaventura, the liurai (king) of Manufahi.

It came after Portugal raised a head tax and pushed forced labour for roads and coffee plantations. Many kingdoms joined. Portuguese troops, with Timorese allies and reinforcements from Mozambique and Macau, crushed it, and thousands of Timorese were killed.

Afterward Portugal broke the power of the liurai and ruled Timor directly. The border with the Dutch half of the island was fixed soon after, completing the shape set by the Treaty of Lisbon. Boaventura is now a national hero. See Dili.
sum: The Manufahi revolt of 1911 and 1912 was the largest uprising against Portuguese rule in Timor, led by Dom Boaventura, the liurai (king) of Manufahi.
